channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-16
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 62 news received.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra helps demonstrate a mathematical construction of the Standard Model
item.description: OpenAI and physicist Nathaniel Craig have published a candidate lattice construction of the Standard Model. GPT-6 Astra reportedly contributed to its development and demonstration.

item.title: Samsung reportedly approached Anthropic and OpenAI to lease its future AI data centers
item.description: Samsung’s IT division reportedly began discussions with Anthropic and OpenAI about becoming tenants of its future artificial intelligence data centers.

item.title: A compromised MCP server can hijack an AI agent’s other tools
item.description: A test cited by VentureBeat indicates that a compromised MCP server prompted an agent connected to five servers to misuse the other tools in 78.3% of cases. The article recommends limiting credentials, adding human validation, and logging the entire call chain.

item.title: Apple is reportedly preparing Siri-controlled smart glasses for 2027
item.description: Apple’s first smart glasses would use Siri to control existing iPhone apps. Apple is reportedly targeting a presentation at WWDC 2027 and a commercial launch at the end of the same year.

item.title: The Atlantic tests ChatGPT on 32,245 personal messages and raises consent questions
item.description: The Atlantic tested ChatGPT on 32,245 personal messages. The experiment raises consent questions when an analysis conducted for one person includes other people’s private conversations.

item.title: Apple launches an AI health study involving 200,000 people
item.description: The Apple Health AI Study app allows U.S. adults aged 21 and older with an iPhone 15 Pro or later to ask health questions. It also provides the peer-reviewed citations associated with the answers.

item.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents pay after approval
item.description: OpenAI is beginning to roll out ChatGPT Wallet. The feature allows an AI agent to pay online securely after the user’s approval.

item.title: Adobe integrates AI agents into Firefly and Creative Cloud creative workflows
item.description: Adobe is introducing new ways to direct the Creative Agent in Firefly and Creative Cloud to handle complex creative tasks while retaining control over the direction and outcome. Users will be able to delegate repetitive tasks, set their preferences, adjust the agent’s plan, and choose which AI models are used.

item.title: ChatGPT Images 2.6 turns product photos into animated GIFs
item.description: OpenAI has added GIF creation to ChatGPT with its Images 2.6 model, using either a prompt or an uploaded photo. The feature can, among other things, animate an element of a product photo, but it is not yet available to all accounts.

item.title: OpenAI invites brands to create verified profiles in ChatGPT
item.description: OpenAI has invited brands to claim free verified profiles in ChatGPT, track how often they are mentioned, and set up AI agents for shoppers.

item.title: The first AI Music Awards rely on humans to portray AI artists
item.description: The first AI Music Awards ceremony was held in Los Angeles, featuring AI presenters, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins. Technical problems interrupted the ceremony several times.

item.title: Nvidia reportedly supplied computing capacity to Chinese companies through Asia
item.description: According to The Wall Street Journal, Nvidia developed partnerships with Asian data centers that leased its advanced chips to Chinese customers. One of these partners reportedly arranged nearly 12 billion dollars’ worth of chip orders in 2024 and 2025.

item.title: Pax Silica countries seek better protection for key AI technologies and supply chains
item.description: Members of Pax Silica, including Japan, Australia, Israel, India, and the United Kingdom, agreed to establish a joint list of AI technologies and supply chains requiring greater protection.

item.title: SK Hynix will invest 1.05 billion dollars in its South Korean suppliers
item.description: SK Hynix has committed to investing approximately 1.05 billion dollars over five years to strengthen Korean suppliers of semiconductor materials, components, and equipment.

item.title: LongCat-2.5 is close behind Claude Opus 5 without using Nvidia chips
item.description: Meituan’s Chinese model scores 88.4 points on Terminal Bench, nearly matching Claude Opus 5, and was reportedly trained entirely on Huawei chips. It combines 1,600 billion parameters, a one-million-token context window, and advanced agent capabilities.

item.title: A robot independently assembles a structure in orbit
item.description: Caltech’s ASTRA robot built a section of an antenna frame in low Earth orbit without an astronaut. This DARPA-supported demonstration is intended to pave the way for much larger space structures.

item.title: Alibaba opens Qwen4-Max Preview for two weeks
item.description: Alibaba is allowing users to test Qwen4-Max Preview until November 25. This multimodal model has a one-million-token context window, agent tools, and compatibility with several development environments.

item.title: Washington is preparing three laws to tighten AI chip exports to China
item.description: Following unproven allegations targeting Jensen Huang, the U.S. Congress is preparing three bills designed to strengthen restrictions on AI chips exported to China. No bill has yet been adopted, and the details of the measures remain unknown.

item.title: A middle-school student invents a water-powered solar tracker
item.description: Jason Chang designed a system costing less than 25 dollars that orients a solar panel using a bucket filled drop by drop, with no motor or electricity. The device produces about 20% more voltage than a fixed panel.

item.title: A Vulcan rocket failure destroys 40 Amazon satellites
item.description: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed about ten minutes after liftoff, destroying 40 satellites belonging to Amazon’s Leo internet network. The cause of the failure remains unknown.

item.title: Confucius4-R2T2 freezes words in live speech transcripts
item.description: This transcription system freezes each word as soon as it appears, without rewriting the beginnings of sentences, while remaining fast and almost as accurate as delayed transcription. It is based on an adaptation of Qwen3-ASR-1.7B trained on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio.

item.title: Apple runs an 816-billion-parameter model on four Mac Studio computers
item.description: The new version of MLX distributes a very large model across several Mac Studio computers connected via Thunderbolt. Muse Spark Open reaches more than 36 tokens per second on four machines, while some models fit on a single 512 GB Mac Studio.

item.title: Alibaba releases its open-source AI code review tool
item.description: Alibaba has open-sourced open-code-review, a tool combining traditional rules with an AI agent to comment on code line by line. It searches in particular for XSS vulnerabilities, SQL injections, and common crashes.

item.title: Claude Cowork lets users launch desktop tasks from a phone
item.description: Claude Cowork can sort files, turn screenshots into spreadsheets, and compile notes into a report. The integration of the desktop and mobile apps lets users launch a task from a phone for execution on a computer.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 paints its images with Python code
item.description: Claude Fable 5.2 generates images by writing Python code that simulates hundreds of thousands of brushstrokes. A photorealistic parking-lot scene reportedly required about 700,000 brushstrokes.

item.title: OATs modules turn connected objects into AI Tamagotchis
item.description: OATs modules display expressions generated by Nano Banana on an E Ink screen based on humidity, light, or motion sensors. These devices cost about 20 dollars and are not yet commercially available.

item.title: Google’s Gemini glasses are available for preorder
item.description: Google is opening preorders for smart glasses designed with Warby Parker, Gentle Monster, and Samsung. They offer translation, directions, and environmental descriptions, with a 12-megapixel camera and nine hours of battery life.

item.title: Agile Robots raises 500 million dollars for its humanoids
item.description: The Munich-based company Agile Robots wants to deploy more industrial robots, particularly in the United States. It raised 500 million dollars from SoftBank and Nvidia to fund its expansion and a possible IPO.

item.title: Apple launches a study on AI use in healthcare
item.description: With OpenEvidence, Apple is offering a study in which participants ask health questions to an AI system relying on recognized medical sources and potentially using their HealthKit data. The study aims to enroll up to 200,000 U.S. participants over the age of 21.

item.title: AI is affecting young workers first, according to an Australian study
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia observes a sharper decline in job postings and employment among 15–24-year-olds in occupations highly exposed to AI. The study remains cautious, as the economic cycle and remote work could also explain the trend.

item.title: Tech job postings plunge as AI appears in half of listings
item.description: The Hacker News monthly job-posting thread contains 244 listings in November, down 37% from a year earlier. AI appears in 51.6% of postings, while junior positions remain around 3%.

item.title: A developer argues that all AI-generated code should be open source
item.description: Jakub Jankiewicz argues that AI-generated code should be open, since the models were trained on free code and Stack Overflow without permission. He also cites the lack of U.S. copyright protection for works created without human intervention.

item.title: YouTube Music and Spotify’s AI hosts disappoint
item.description: A Wired journalist tested YouTube Music and Spotify’s AI hosts and found empty commentary as well as several errors. She ultimately disabled the feature.

item.title: In Singapore, 94% of small-business owners are asking for AI help
item.description: According to a YouGov study commissioned by Meta, 94% of surveyed small-business owners in Singapore want more support using AI. Meta trained more than 180 merchants and creators during its Meta Upskill Day 2026.

item.title: Jensen Huang is reportedly considering taking over Nvidia again
item.description: A few days after his resignation linked to the scandal, Jensen Huang reportedly discussed returning to lead Nvidia with people close to him, according to the Financial Times as relayed by Bloomberg. No official confirmation or timeline has been provided.

item.title: Older connected devices remain a major network vulnerability
item.description: According to Cisco, nearly 40% of the most exploited vulnerabilities affect end-of-life hardware, including routers and cameras that no longer receive updates. Cisco recommends regularly replacing this equipment, but few brands disclose their support lifespans.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO becomes a test for the entire AI sector
item.description: The creator of Claude is set to list on the Nasdaq at between 70 and 78 dollars per share, amid a difficult environment for AI and Nvidia. Anthropic expects more than 900 billion dollars in supplier spending, despite a loss of 104 billion over nine months.

item.title: An AI learns words using a sleep-inspired method
item.description: Princeton researchers trained an AI using recordings of a baby’s daily life. Regularly replaying recent memories enabled it to recognize thousands of words, whereas it had recognized none before.

item.title: Oakland employees negotiate AI protections
item.description: A tentative agreement provides that the city must retrain or reassign employees whose jobs would be eliminated by AI. The agreement also includes a 9% pay increase over three years and helped avert a strike.

item.title: Claude Sheets automatically compares two quotes
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Sheets in beta for its paid plans. The tool creates an editable spreadsheet with formulas to compare rates, quantities, and recurring costs.

item.title: Mister Blocks turns a photo of LEGO bricks into building ideas
item.description: Mister Blocks analyzes a photo of loose LEGO bricks and suggests builds that can be made with the available pieces. The service also provides rotatable 3D instructions.

item.title: MIT improves a small model by having another AI correct it
item.description: MIT researchers used one AI to correct another, much as developers fix software. The small model’s score on a math test rose from 8% to 48% without retraining.

item.title: Notion alerts customers after access keys leak at Fireworks
item.description: Notion warned companies that access keys issued by its services had been exposed during a breach at Fireworks, its AI provider.

item.title: LangChain reportedly raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation
item.description: LangChain, which helps developers build AI agents, reportedly raised $300 million in a deal valuing the company at $3 billion.

item.title: Harvard publishes a guide on AI’s effects by learner age
item.description: Harvard researchers published a guide explaining when AI can help or hinder learning at different ages.

item.title: Jensen Huang steps down as NVIDIA CEO after 33 years
item.description: Jensen Huang has stepped down as NVIDIA’s CEO after 33 years. The planned succession and its implications for the company are at the center of questions.

item.title: Anthropic releases two versions of its Fable and Mythos models
item.description: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, two versions of the same model with different safety rules.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches AlphaGenome 2 to predict the effects of DNA mutations
item.description: AlphaGenome 2 predicts why the same DNA change may affect one cell type but not another.

item.title: United Airlines bans unauthorized AI agents from booking flights
item.description: United Airlines has banned unauthorized AI agents from booking flights, citing risks including accidental purchases and the misuse of miles.

item.title: Google DeepMind uses AI to verify Signal’s code
item.description: Google DeepMind used AI agents to mathematically prove that Signal’s code provides some of its privacy protections.

item.title: Building your first AI automation
item.description: Automation consists of a trigger, an action, and an outcome. It is recommended to start with a low-risk task so that an error has no consequences.

item.title: Five questions to identify tasks to automate
item.description: After creating a first automation, five questions can help determine which tasks are worth delegating to AI.

item.title: Automating your inbox and calendar
item.description: AI can prepare email and calendar actions up to the send button. Sending messages and accepting meetings, however, remain under the user’s control.

item.title: Adobe prepares local MCP integrations to edit native files
item.description: Adobe has unveiled local MCP integrations that let third-party agents connect to Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects to directly edit native project files while keeping them editable. These integrations will be offered in private beta in early 2027.

item.title: A dermatologist recommends skipping face washing
item.description: A dermatologist says your skin might thank you for not washing your face.

item.title: Ring launches a home security drone and patrol robot
item.description: Ring has launched Ring Robotics with the Ring Drone Cam, a $270 indoor flying camera, and the Ring Rover Cam, a $1,000 patrol robot designed for businesses. The drone can travel to the source of an alarm, and the robot can follow preset routes, but these cameras raise privacy concerns.

item.title: Agility goes public as the first publicly traded humanoid company
item.description: Agility has gone public on the Nasdaq as the first publicly traded company specializing in humanoid robots, with a pre-money valuation of $2.5 billion. However, it generated just $1.8 million in revenue last year.

item.title: Business Insider unveils its 2026 Rising Stars of Wall Street
item.description: Business Insider has presented its 2026 selection of Wall Street Rising Stars, highlighting the people shaping the future of finance.

item.title: Goldman Sachs names 109 new partners
item.description: Goldman Sachs has named 109 new partners, its largest class since 2010.

item.title: Skydance reshuffles power after its merger with Paramount-WBD
item.description: Business Insider examines Skydance’s new leadership and the shifts in power following its merger with Paramount-WBD.

item.title: China-based executives gain power at TikTok
item.description: Business Insider analyzes how China-based executives have gained power at TikTok Shop.

item.title: Disney employees question leaders about layoffs
item.description: At Disney, employees pressed their leaders about potential layoffs as uncertainty weighed on team morale.
